## Result

- Skill: design-review
- Review ID and round: design-review-r4
- Judgment: changes-requested
- Exact package: Design, System, Workflow and retained Target-Native Init amendment (four stored subjects).
- Resolved prior findings: des-review-f2, des-review-f3, des-review-f4, by their original reporter; des-review-f1 remains resolved.
- New material finding: des-review-f5, primary-agent/design correction in the retained installation-owner specification.
- Upstream basis: unchanged accepted proposal and independent proposal-review.
- Isolation: no activity/routing change, model edits or downstream readiness claim.

## Whole-package assessment

The complete corrected models and retained installer specification were independently assessed against the original review basis and directly affected source contracts. The bounded model responsibilities, current/shared ownership, method-source/ADR migration map, preserved example safeguards, product-direction authority, independent Review and Test policy, conditional public resources and representative local/integrated acceptance intent remain coherent. No repository-wide consolidation, new gate/schema/service, publication or customer adoption is inferred. The new installer member is a substantive scoped amendment of the unmigrated installation responsibility, correctly requiring retained boundary-first-v1 feature-format adoption for TNI-DES-01–06 rather than a claim of model consolidation or unchanged historical approval. Its original body and approval remain distinct.

The three reported corrections are adequate at Design level. However, two newly authored example ownership rows contradict that retained format's normative governing relation. This is an actionable exact-authority mismatch, so the ordered judgment is changes-requested, not approved or inconclusive. Previous review judgments and immutable finding origins remain historical; resolving their findings does not make the earlier package approval current.

## Reporter-owned dispositions

- des-review-f2: Resolved at the Design contract level. Design now consumes the retained installation owner amendment TNI-DES-01–06, which checks original complete locked roots before replacement, names the narrowly extended --write-state path, requires external backup and authorization, protects neighbors and modified content, stages/verifies before state publication, and specifies caught-failure/interruption recovery with exclusive basis or intervening-write preservation. System composition and E-DES-01–04 expose clean, modified and interrupted outcomes. No claim that this future installer behavior is implemented or executed. The separate new boundary-table finding does not restore the former cleanup trap.

- des-review-f3: Resolved. Exact conditional packaged resources now name boundary-first-method-v1, boundary-first-feature-authoring-v1 and legacy-technical-authoring alongside legacy-source-reconciliation, with required legacy architecture/ADR assets inside the skill. Repository templates are contributor-only. The contract distinguishes missing project authority from missing package guidance and specifies substantive installed legacy amendment without internal checkout, retired skills or forced migration. This settles the Design dependency closure; actual package generation/installation proof remains downstream.

- des-review-f4: Resolved. Workflow adoption support row explicitly assigns the retained mapping to Design, with Workflow consuming it for coordination and Delivery verifying affected consumers. This agrees with WF-SR-07 and Design replacement ownership, preserving retained retirement scope without a second current owner.

## Finding des-review-f5

Material; artifact-local, retained installation-owner specification; correction stage design. Location: specs/target-native-init.md, Example ownership E-DES-01 and E-DES-04. This amendment expressly adopts boundary-first-v1. Approved PBF-R024 and the compact boundary method require every cited example requirement to be governed by every cited boundary. E-DES-01 cites TNI-DES-01/02/04 with INPUT-001 (01/02), STATE-001 (02/04/05) and COMPOSE-001 (01/02/04/06); INPUT does not govern04 and STATE does not govern01. E-DES-04 cites02/03/05 while STATE/TEMPORAL do not govern03 and AUTH does not govern05. Consequently these rows claim ownership relationships absent from their boundary definitions. The validator passes because its current example check only requires overlap with each boundary; that structural result is weaker than the retained normative rule and does not settle this semantic mismatch.

Required outcome and safe resolution: Reconcile these example ownership rows with PBF-R024 while preserving all stated acceptance outcomes and their genuine requirement owners. Use honest separate governed illustrations/subcases or boundary references whose governing sets actually cover the cited requirements; do not add fictitious boundary ownership just to satisfy a table check. Keep composed hazards in Selected interactions. This is a bounded author-owned specification correction, not a request to change validator semantics, installation behavior or the governing boundary method in this initiative. Independently reassess the exact resulting package.

## Evidence and limitations

Independent boundary validation of all four files passed structurally, but source inspection identified the weaker overlap implementation and the PBF-R024 semantic mismatch above. Author evidence records three-model prose pass, four-file readability pass with 241 warnings, 79 resolving relative links and unchanged historical installer body. The full four-file prose command remains failed/current with 13 original mid-sentence wrapping errors; the exact baseline comparison records no new errors. This is retained historical formatting debt, not a full prose pass or a reason to erase the failed evidence. No adapter, installer, fault recovery or implementation tests were executed by this Design assessment. Delivery must allocate those concrete checks; this review judges contract coherence and feasibility, not realization. Record-store validation and git diff --check are run after saving. Prior direct-source/no-project-map rationale remains.

## Independence provenance

Independent nonauthor task /root/independent_design_review reassessed the exact four-member package and prior findings after primary-agent authored the corrections. Reviewer authored no governed model or installer specification and changed no implementation or routing. Author self-checks are evidence only; source and semantic assessment are reviewer-owned.
